items.question: What is WJP full-color 3D printing?
items.answer: WJP (Wax Jet Printing) is an industrial-grade full-color 3D printing process using wax-jet + curing. It directly prints 16-million-color models with no post-processing coloring needed. High color fidelity and fine texture — perfect for portraits, pets, anime characters, and any scene that needs color and detail preserved.

items.question: Can I really order just one piece? Any minimum?
items.answer: Absolutely. One-piece minimum, no MOQ. Our production line is purpose-built for single-piece / small-batch customization — every order handled individually from start to finish. Bulk orders (30+) enjoy group pricing — see the Pricing page.

items.question: How long until I receive my order?
items.answer: Standard orders deliver in 5-7 working days (excluding remote areas). Process: 24h 3D proof → customer approval → 48-72h WJP printing → Express shipping dispatch. Rush service: contact customer support.

items.question: Is one photo enough? Do I need professional images?
items.answer: A single front photo works, but the result may be slightly less ideal. We recommend 3-5 photos from different angles (front + side + back / top). AI-generated images, illustrations, and anime reference sheets are all accepted.

items.question: What products can I order? Any size limits?
items.answer: Pet badges (~30-50mm), keychains (~40-60mm), fridge magnets (~60-100mm), figures (~100-200mm), standees (~150-300mm) all supported. For over 200mm or complex shapes, please contact customer support for evaluation.

items.question: Who owns the 3D model files?
items.answer: You do. After modeling is complete, we provide STL / OBJ files for download. You can use them for personal collection, re-printing, or commercial sublicensing. We retain no copyright and will not resell your work.

items.question: What if I'm not satisfied with the final product?
items.answer: At the 3D proof stage, one free revision; full refund if you reject the proof entirely. At the printing stage, defects (color loss, breakage, etc.) are remade free or refunded in full. Shipping damage is replaced free with packaging photos.

items.question: Which payment methods are supported? Invoices available?
items.answer: WeChat Pay, Alipay, and corporate bank transfer. Business customers can apply for VAT ordinary invoices or special invoices — contact customer support to register.

intro.title: Upload a model, get its weight
intro.body: Parses the model's bounding box and volume, converts them to resin weight with the material density, and suggests the best print orientation together with a support weight estimate. Everything runs in your browser — model files are never uploaded and results are never stored.

calibration.hint: Support weight = full-wrap weight − model weight = wrap-support volume × fill rate × density. The full wrap is the whole block from the platform up to the top of the model (support + model); the wrap support is that block minus the model itself — the same thing the model checker draws; the fill rate is the solid fraction of the support (the support is solid, 100% by default) and the density is the material's own weight density.
calibration.oneClickDesc: Enter the measured support weight to back-solve the fill rate.

manual.weightHint: The solid volume is estimated from the envelope size and the solid ratio, then multiplied by the material density.

dialog.title: Model settings · {name}

dialog.adjustHint: Changing a dimension scales volume and surface area proportionally, and the weight follows.

algorithm.title: How the weight is calculated
algorithm.p1: Resin weight = solid volume × material density. The solid volume comes from the model's bounding box scaled by the fill ratio; in manual mode it is estimated from the envelope size × fill ratio.
algorithm.formula: Weight = solid volume (cm³) × material density ({density} g/cm³)
algorithm.p2: Support weight = full-wrap weight − model weight: the full wrap is the whole block you get before the support is washed off (support + model), so weighing that block and subtracting the model leaves the support. The support weight is estimated from the fill rate and the support resin density (the wrap support volume is the same one the model checker computes), and the total weight = material weight + support weight; use “Support weight calibration” to back-solve it from a measured weight. The optimizer picks the pose with the least support and the lowest layer height.

normals.note: Slicers rely on normals to tell inside from outside. Inverted normals make slicing fail or produce a hollow part — run a “recalculate normals” pass to fix it.

badEdges.note: An open mesh cannot be sliced correctly: planar holes can be filled with a flat patch, cracks need bridging. Keep the normals pointing outward after repairing.

shells.cavityNote: Support inside a sealed cavity can never be washed out completely; the residue ruins the finish and can burst thin walls as it swells. WJP full color does not support hollow designs — delete the inner shell and make the model solid.
shells.noiseNote: Noise shells are usually modelling leftovers or tessellation artefacts. They print as loose blobs — delete them and re-export (toggle “noise shells” under the viewport to locate them).

overview.note: Turn on “wrap-around support” below the viewport to preview the water-soluble support shell and the platform footprint: the model drops onto the platform and everything between platform and model is support material (WJP jets layer by layer, so there is no overhang). It is washed off after printing. Issue legend entries only appear when that issue was actually detected.

sidebar.unitsNote: Coordinates are in mm (the 3D printing convention); the print direction is +Z.

wjp.scope: Scope: inverted normals / broken edges and faces / shells and watertightness. Overhangs are carried by the water-soluble support and wall thickness is guaranteed by solid infill, so neither is checked.

fail.summary: {critical} critical issue(s) found — repair them before slicing.

risk.summary: No critical issues, but {warning} item(s) need attention.

pass.summary: No inverted normals, broken faces or shell problems found — you can slice this straight away.

globalInverted.title: {count} closed shell(s) are inverted inside-out
globalInverted.detail: The whole shell faces inward, so the slicer reads inside and outside as swapped and cuts a hollow part.
globalInverted.advice: Run “recalculate / unify normals” on the whole model in your modelling software, then export again.

localFlipped.title: {count} face(s) wound against their neighbours
localFlipped.detail: Faces with reversed winding produce broken or self-intersecting slices.
localFlipped.advice: Fix with “unify normals”; if they persist, look for zero-thickness or overlapping faces at that spot.

ok.title: Normals look correct
ok.detail: No inverted shells and no locally flipped faces were detected.

notClosed.title: Mesh is not closed: {openEdges} open edge(s) ({planarHoles} planar hole(s), {cracks} crack(s) / tear(s))
notClosed.detail: The mesh has unclosed boundaries. WJP slicing needs a watertight mesh: open borders are cut into notches or break volume computation, so the part cannot be printed. Planar holes can be filled with a flat patch; cracks and tears need bridging.
notClosed.advice: Run “close holes / fill holes” in a mesh repair tool and re-export — keep the normals pointing outward while you do it.

ok.title: Mesh is closed
ok.detail: No open edges — the model is watertight.

issues.title: Bad faces: {degenerate} degenerate, {duplicate} duplicate pair(s), {nonManifold} non-manifold edge(s)
issues.detail: Degenerate faces (zero area), duplicate faces (coinciding with another face) and non-manifold edges (an edge shared by three or more faces) skew volume and surface area, and slicers often fail on them outright.
issues.advice: Run a “check / repair mesh” pass in your modelling software (merge duplicate vertices, delete duplicate faces, re-triangulate), then export.

ok.title: No bad faces
ok.detail: No degenerate faces, duplicate faces or non-manifold edges were detected.

sealedHollow.title: {count} sealed cavity/cavities inside the model
sealedHollow.detail: A closed inner shell is trapped inside the outer one. Water-soluble support cannot be washed out of a sealed cavity — the residue bursts thin walls as it swells.
sealedHollow.advice: WJP full color is solid infill and does not support hollow designs: delete the inner shell and leave a single solid shell.

enclosedOpen.title: {count} enclosed fragment shell(s)
enclosedOpen.detail: Unclosed leftover geometry is trapped inside the outer shell — support will be left behind there too.
enclosedOpen.advice: Delete the inner fragments and export again.

noise.title: {count} noise fragment shell(s)
noise.detail: The model contains {components} disconnected shells, {count} of them tiny relative to the whole. These are usually modelling leftovers or tessellation noise, and they print as loose blobs.
noise.advice: Toggle “noise shells” under the viewport to locate them, delete them and re-export.

ok.title: Shell structure looks correct
ok.detail: No sealed cavities and no enclosed fragment geometry were detected.

multiple.title: {count} separate part(s)
multiple.detail: The model is made of {count} disconnected shells. Leave about {assemblyGap} mm clearance on static assembly faces and {movingGap} mm on moving or sliding fits.
multiple.advice: Confirm this is intentional multi-part design; if the parts only came apart during export, merge them into one shell.

size.title: Bounding size {dx} × {dy} × {dz} mm
size.detail: At this size the WJP full-color tolerance is roughly ±{tol} mm. The material deflects between {heatMin} and {heatMax} °C, so slender parts should be stiffened.
size.advice: Leave tolerance margin on critical fit dimensions instead of ordering to nominal size.

warnings.openEdges: The mesh is not closed: {openEdges} open edge(s), {planarHoles} planar hole(s), {cracks} crack(s) / tear(s).
warnings.flippedFaces: {count} face(s) are wound against their neighbours.
warnings.sealedHollow: {count} sealed cavity/cavities detected — support inside them cannot be washed out.
warnings.enclosedOpenShells: {count} fragment shell(s) trapped inside the outer shell.
